issues.message: The root picture says that the doubled ض gives حَضَّ a sense of pressing or urging. A shadda marks gemination; it does not by itself supply the lexical meaning or force. This is a misleading learner shortcut.
issues.requiredAction: Replace the claim with a neutral mnemonic or with the attested lexical gloss, and explain the shadda only as the doubled final radical if that recognition clue is retained.

evidence.draftText: The doubled ض gives the root a sense of pressing or urging.
evidence.morphology: The draft itself identifies a geminate root ح ض ض.

issues.message: The س ك ن connection is presented as if stillness or restricted movement explains the lexical meaning of مِسْكِين. That can make a speculative memory aid look like a reliable derivation.
issues.requiredAction: Label any root association explicitly as a mnemonic only, or replace it with the reviewed lexical meaning needy/poor person without implying that inability to move is the word's derivation.

evidence.draftText: The root connection س ك ن can suggest being restricted or unable to move freely, a useful memory aid for neediness.
evidence.learnerRisk: A learner may memorize an unsupported etymology instead of the contextual lexical meaning.

issues.message: The ayah-level grammar explanation introduces مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ without an English gloss, while the word lessons use iḍāfah plus English explanations. This creates an avoidable terminology jump for learners.
issues.requiredAction: Gloss the term at first use, for example second term of an iḍāfah/genitive construction, and use the same transliteration and English label in the ayah and word layers.

evidence.draftText: ٱلْمِسْكِينِ is its genitive مُضَافٌ إِلَيْهِ.
evidence.relatedTeaching: The word lesson calls it the second term of an iḍāfah.

issues.message: The recognition clue calls فَ emphatic and instructs the learner to hear a pause after it. فَ is a short consequence connector, not an emphatic consonant, and it does not impose a pause here.
issues.requiredAction: Replace the cue with a visual/grammatical recognition clue such as identifying فَ as a consequence connector and ٌ as tanwīn ḍammah on وَيْلٌ; do not prescribe a pause after فَ.

evidence.draftText: Hear the pause after the emphatic فَ and notice the tanwīn at the end of وَيْلٌ.
evidence.learnerRisk: The learner may pronounce فَ as emphatic or insert a pause that is not part of the connector's function.
